sources.researchNote: The Bundesarchiv dates the photograph to about 1930. The signal tower on Potsdamer Platz stood from 1924 to 1937, which agrees with that date. The image stands for the city in Kaper’s Berlin years; it does not show a place connected with him.

media.title: Leipziger Platz and Leipziger Straße, Berlin — photograph, c. 1930
media.description: View from above across Potsdamer Platz towards Leipziger Platz and Leipziger Straße in about 1930, with the traffic-signal tower of 1924 in the foreground, one of Schinkel’s gatehouses of the Potsdam Gate behind it, and trams running into Leipziger Straße. The Bundesarchiv records the photographer as A. Frankl.
media.altText: Black-and-white street view from above of a busy Berlin square with a clock-topped traffic tower, trams, cyclists and pedestrians, a classical gatehouse among trees and a long avenue of large buildings beyond.
media.publicCaption: Berlin about 1930: Potsdamer Platz with its traffic tower, looking into Leipziger Platz and Leipziger Straße.

places.publicNote: Berlin was Kaper’s principal city during his German period, associated with his studies, cabaret and publishing networks, and early film work.
